name: Tasimelteon
lead: Tasimelteon is a prescription melatonin MT1/MT2 receptor agonist developed by Vanda Pharmaceuticals and sold as Hetlioz. The US FDA approved it in January 2014 for Non-24-Hour Sleep-Wake Disorder in adults, and in December 2020 for nighttime sleep disturbances in Smith-Magenis syndrome [1][2].

Non-24 is a circadian rhythm disorder mainly affecting totally blind people. Tasimelteon is not a general insomnia or appearance product. No published study has examined it for appearance, and no looksmaxxing community material about it was found.
Phase 3 trials in totally blind people (SET and RESET) reported entrainment of the circadian rhythm in a minority of patients on treatment [3][4].

paras: The US label indicates tasimelteon for Non-24-Hour Sleep-Wake Disorder in adults [2]. A later approval covers nighttime sleep disturbance in Smith-Magenis syndrome in patients aged 3 and older [1]. The label states that the mechanism by which it works in Non-24 is unclear but that MT1 and MT2 receptors are thought to be involved in controlling circadian rhythms [2].

The most common reactions on the label (above 5% and at least twice as frequent as with placebo) were headache, raised alanine aminotransferase, nightmares or unusual dreams, and upper respiratory or urinary tract infection [2]. The label warns of somnolence and advises patients to limit activity after taking it [2]. Postmarketing pregnancy reports are insufficient to assess risk [2].

Tasimelteon is an agonist at MT1 and MT2 receptors, which are densely expressed in the brain's circadian pacemaker [2][5]. It is metabolised mainly by CYP1A2 and CYP3A4, and dedicated pharmacokinetic studies examined renal and hepatic impairment, smoking and interacting drugs [1][6][7][8].

Two randomised placebo-controlled phase 3 trials, SET and RESET, studied totally blind people with Non-24 and were published in The Lancet in 2015 [3]. Earlier phase 2 and phase 3 trials examined transient insomnia after a shift in sleep time in healthy volunteers [4]. Further registered trials include phase 1 pharmacokinetic studies and a paediatric study [6][7][9]. A small early-phase trial in REM sleep behaviour disorder was terminated [10]. No studies were found on tasimelteon for appearance outcomes.

timeline.event: FDA approves Hetlioz for Non-24-Hour Sleep-Wake Disorder [1].
SET and RESET phase 3 results published in The Lancet [3].
Approval extended to Smith-Magenis syndrome sleep disturbance [1].

card.summary: A prescription circadian drug approved for non-24-hour disorder in blind people; no appearance evidence.
card.note: Approved only for Non-24 and Smith-Magenis sleep disturbance.

quick.overview:
Tasimelteon is a melatonin-receptor drug approved in the US for Non-24-Hour Sleep-Wake Disorder, mainly seen in totally blind people, and for sleep problems in Smith-Magenis syndrome.

It is not an insomnia pill in general, and no research ties it to appearance.
quick.mechanism: It activates MT1 and MT2 melatonin receptors involved in circadian timing; the label says exactly how it works in Non-24 is unclear.
quick.risks: Reported effects include headache, raised liver enzyme ALT, vivid dreams or nightmares and infections. The label warns of somnolence. It is prescription-only.
